prompt: Build a check report on the June 2024 order lines. These tables may hold errors. June 2024 means order_ts, as stored, from 1 June 2024 up to but not including 1 July 2024. Return one row for each of three checks, with four columns, in this order: check_name; n_bad; bad_share, n_bad divided by the number of June 2024 lines as stored, a fraction from 0 to 1, not rounded; and result, 'pass' when n_bad is 0, otherwise 'fail'. The checks are 'resent_copies', the lines that are resent copies (two lines are copies of one order line when order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id and line_discount_eur all match, with a missing promo_id matching a missing one; every line beyond the first of such a set is a resent copy); 'price_in_cents', the lines whose unit_price_eur is more than 10 times the product's unit_cost_eur; and 'unknown_product', the lines whose product_id is not in products. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, divide each check's count by the number of June 2024 lines.
The denominator is one number for every check, so a scalar subquery on the June lines works, wrapped in NULLIF(..., 0) and divided with /.
why_this_works: Each check counts its own rule over the same June lines, and dividing by their number puts the checks on one scale.
